question: Why does the frozen dual-pose readout lose Acc@50 on pedestrians and cyclists, and can its vehicle gains coexist with a suitable fallback?
cohort: The same 9310 previously exposed Ordinary Validation descriptions and exact Qwen replies from 824b6a48bf7db54a4678296bb11ee78586d31838
primary_metric: Upright oriented IoU > 0.50 on all descriptions, plus Acc@25 and mIoU, by category, platform, category-platform and recording
diagnosis: Use H and C_pca to exchange horizontal center, horizontal extent, vertical interval and yaw. Rebuild an H-rule box on the exact C fit support to isolate support and terrain from the anchor change.

arms.F_complete: Original measured_box and complete on the same isolation-side support as C_pca
arms.B_pca: Original fit support and PCA pose. Expand the Qwen prior to at least the measured span in that pose, then reanchor.
arms.B_ray: The same measured lower bounds in both poses, with the original independent rays and clipping scale
arms.C_ray_applicable: Retain the original two-pose instance and independent ray score only if both valid frozen outputs identify a road motor vehicle and the existing independent-ray eligibility is satisfied. In other cases use H. Apply the same rule across platforms.
arms.C_ray_shuffled: Permute the applicable flags among ray-eligible descriptions within each recording with a fixed seed, preserving activation count

category_features: A fixed allowlist of common road-motor-vehicle head terms in the two already produced Qwen label fields. A conflicting human, bicycle, motorcycle, or animal term invalidates a vehicle label. Ground-truth categories are reserved for post-seal diagnosis and reporting.
selection_rule: Prefer a repair that restores H on pedestrians and cyclists in pooled Acc@50 and retains most of the original vehicle gain, with all losses and recording-level uncertainty reported. Compare against a count-matched shuffled route and retain the physical-width alternative as a control. Decide within this exposed benchmark.
